title: Leviticus Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 19.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:2, why are the children of Israel commanded to be holy?
options: Because I the LORD your God am holy
Because it is the tradition of their fathers
Because it will bring them wealth
Because the priests said so
questions.correctAnswer: Because I the LORD your God am holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:2 states that the children of Israel shall be holy because the LORD their God is holy.

questions.question: What are men specifically instructed to fear in Leviticus 19:3?
options: Their mother and father
The priests and elders
The king and his army
Strangers and foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: Their mother and father
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:3 commands every man to fear his mother and father and keep the sabbaths.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 19:4 forbid the children of Israel from doing?
options: Turning to idols and making molten gods
Eating unclean animals
Telling lies
Working on the sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Turning to idols and making molten gods
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:4 prohibits turning unto idols and making molten gods, affirming the LORD as their God.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:5 states that peace offerings must be offered by command of the priests.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:5 says peace offerings shall be offered at the offerer's own will, not by priestly command.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:6, by when must the peace offering be eaten?
options: The same day and the next day
Within one week
After three days
Only on the seventh day
questions.correctAnswer: The same day and the next day
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:6 instructs that the peace offering be eaten on the day it is offered and the following day.

questions.question: What happens if the peace offering is eaten on the third day according to Leviticus 19:7?
options: It is abominable and not accepted
It is blessed by the priest
It is considered holy
It is forgiven by God
questions.correctAnswer: It is abominable and not accepted
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:7 states that if eaten on the third day, the offering is abominable and not accepted.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:8 teaches that anyone who eats the peace offering on the third day bears their iniquity and shall be cut off.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:8 clearly states that eating the offering after the prescribed time profanes the LORD’s thing and the soul shall be cut off from among his people.

questions.question: When reaping the harvest of your land, what does Leviticus 19:9 command regarding the corners of your field?
options: Do not wholly reap the corners
Reap all corners thoroughly
Burn the corners of the field
Plant a new crop in the corners
questions.correctAnswer: Do not wholly reap the corners
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:9 commands not to wholly reap the corners of the field or gather the gleanings, leaving them for the poor.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:10, who should be left with the gleanings of the vineyard?
options: The poor and the stranger
The priests
The king
The elders
questions.correctAnswer: The poor and the stranger
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:10 instructs to leave the gleanings and grapes for the poor and the stranger as the LORD your God commands.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:11 commands that stealing and lying to one another are forbidden.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:11 explicitly forbids stealing, dealing falsely, and lying one to another.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 19:12 warn against doing with God's name?
options: Swearing falsely and profaning the name
Blessing others
Singing praises
Teaching children
questions.correctAnswer: Swearing falsely and profaning the name
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:12 warns not to swear falsely by God's name or profane it, affirming the LORD’s authority.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:13, what must not happen to the wages of a hired man?
options: They shall not abide with you all night until morning
They may be delayed for a week
They must be paid in goods
They are to be given to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not abide with you all night until morning
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:13 commands that the wages of a hired man must be paid without delay and not kept overnight.

questions.question: In Leviticus 19:1-13, which instruction appears first?
options: Ye shall be holy
Ye shall not steal
Ye shall not turn unto idols
Ye shall fear every man his mother and father
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall be holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:2 is the first command given in this passage instructing the children of Israel to be holy because God is holy.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:3 commands keeping the sabbaths as part of fearing father and mother.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:3 commands every man to fear his parents and keep the sabbaths, linking these duties together.

questions.question: What consequence does Leviticus 19:8 state for those who eat the peace offering after the allowed time?
options: The soul shall be cut off from among his people
They shall be forgiven immediately
They must offer a double sacrifice
They shall be given a warning
questions.correctAnswer: The soul shall be cut off from among his people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:8 warns that eating the peace offering after the prescribed time profanes the LORD’s thing and the soul will be cut off.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:14, what specific actions are forbidden in relation to the deaf and the blind?
options: Curse the deaf and put a stumblingblock before the blind
Ignore the deaf and blind
Help the deaf but not the blind
Only speak kindly to the deaf and blind
questions.correctAnswer: Curse the deaf and put a stumblingblock before the blind
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:14 explicitly forbids cursing the deaf and putting a stumblingblock before the blind, teaching respect and care for vulnerable individuals. This connects with fearing God as stated in the same verse.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 19:15 instruct judges to conduct themselves in judgment?
options: Judge without respect to persons, whether poor or mighty
Favor the mighty over the poor
Give preferential treatment to the poor
Judge according to popular opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Judge without respect to persons, whether poor or mighty
questions.explanation: Verse 15 commands judges to act righteously without partiality, respecting neither the poor nor the mighty, which upholds justice as a reflection of God's holiness (Leviticus 19:15).

questions.question: What behavior is prohibited in Leviticus 19:16 regarding gossip and harm to neighbors?
options: Going about as a talebearer and standing against the blood of a neighbor
Speaking only the truth about neighbors
Helping neighbors reconcile conflicts
Keeping silent about wrongs done to neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: Going about as a talebearer and standing against the blood of a neighbor
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:16 forbids spreading harmful reports (talebearing) and failing to protect neighbors, emphasizing responsibility to prevent harm and promote community well-being.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:17, what should one do when a brother sins?
options: Rebuke the neighbor and not allow sin to remain upon him
Ignore the sin to maintain peace
Seek revenge in secret
Report the sin publicly without warning
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuke the neighbor and not allow sin to remain upon him
questions.explanation: Verse 17 teaches that hatred in the heart is wrong and instructs believers to lovingly rebuke neighbors to prevent sin from continuing, promoting accountability.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 19:18 describe the proper attitude toward others?
options: Love your neighbor as yourself and do not avenge or bear a grudge
Love only those who love you
Seek revenge against enemies
Bear grudges for justice
questions.correctAnswer: Love your neighbor as yourself and do not avenge or bear a grudge
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:18 commands loving neighbors as oneself and forbids vengeance or grudges, highlighting forgiveness and mercy as key virtues.

questions.question: What three prohibitions does Leviticus 19:19 give concerning animals, fields, and garments?
options: No crossbreeding cattle, no sowing mixed seeds, no wearing garments of linen and wool
No mixing water and wine, no planting trees near fields, no wearing dyed clothes
No using iron tools on trees, no eating mixed grains, no shaving the head
No sacrificing mixed animals, no planting during Sabbath, no wearing leather clothing
questions.correctAnswer: No crossbreeding cattle, no sowing mixed seeds, no wearing garments of linen and wool
questions.explanation: Verse 19 lists three specific prohibitions related to maintaining purity in livestock breeding, agriculture, and clothing, emphasizing obedience to God's statutes.

questions.question: What penalty is given in Leviticus 19:20 for lying carnally with a bondmaid betrothed to a husband who is not free?
options: She shall be scourged; they shall not be put to death
They shall both be put to death
She shall be sold as a slave
They shall be excommunicated
questions.correctAnswer: She shall be scourged; they shall not be put to death
questions.explanation: Verse 20 specifies scourging for the woman, but no death penalty, because she was not free, reflecting nuanced justice for bondmaids.

questions.question: What offering must the man bring according to Leviticus 19:21 after committing the trespass described in verse 20?
options: A ram as a trespass offering to the LORD
A lamb burnt offering
A grain offering
A sin offering of goats
questions.correctAnswer: A ram as a trespass offering to the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 21 instructs bringing a ram for a trespass offering to make atonement for the sin committed, linking to the previous verse's sin.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 19:22 describe the priest's role after the trespass offering is brought?
options: The priest shall make atonement and forgive the sin
The priest shall reject the offering
The priest shall offer the sacrifice to the people
The priest shall punish the sinner
questions.correctAnswer: The priest shall make atonement and forgive the sin
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states the priest makes atonement with the ram and the sin is forgiven, showing the priest’s mediating role between God and sinner.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:23-25, what is the timeline for eating fruit from newly planted trees?
options: Do not eat for three years; the fourth year the fruit is holy; eat in the fifth year
Eat immediately after planting; bless the fruit yearly
Eat the fruit in the first year only
Ignore the fruit for seven years
questions.correctAnswer: Do not eat for three years; the fourth year the fruit is holy; eat in the fifth year
questions.explanation: Verses 23 to 25 explain the fruit is considered uncircumcised and not to be eaten for three years; the fourth-year fruit is holy to praise God; and the fifth-year fruit may be eaten to yield increase.

questions.question: What two prohibitions are given in Leviticus 19:26 regarding consumption and practices?
options: Do not eat blood; do not use enchantments or observe times
Do not eat meat; do not pray on holy days
Do not drink wine; do not fast
Do not eat fruit; do not cut hair
questions.correctAnswer: Do not eat blood; do not use enchantments or observe times
questions.explanation: Verse 26 prohibits consuming blood and engaging in enchantment or observing times, emphasizing purity and trust in God rather than occult practices.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:27, what physical grooming practices are forbidden?
options: Rounding the corners of the head and marring the corners of the beard
Cutting the hair short and shaving the whole body
Dyeing the hair and beard
Plucking eyebrows and shaving the neck
questions.correctAnswer: Rounding the corners of the head and marring the corners of the beard
questions.explanation: Verse 27 forbids certain hair and beard grooming practices, reflecting the call to maintain distinctions set by God in appearance.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 19:28 forbid in relation to marks on the body?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 28 forbids making cuttings in flesh or printing marks on the body, emphasizing sanctity of the body as given by God.

questions.question: Leviticus 19:29 warns against prostituting one's daughter to cause wickedness in the land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 29 explicitly forbids prostituting a daughter to avoid wickedness spreading in the land, indicating the importance of moral purity in the community.

questions.question: Leviticus 19:30 instructs to keep the sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary as a way to honor God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:30 commands keeping sabbaths and reverencing the sanctuary as an expression of fearing the LORD, not merely honoring Him; the correct focus is fear and reverence, not just honor.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 19.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:27, what specific physical alteration is prohibited?
options: Rounding the corners of your heads
Shaving the entire head
Cutting the hair short all over
Dyeing the hair
questions.correctAnswer: Rounding the corners of your heads
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:27 explicitly states, 'Ye shall not round the corners of your heads, neither shalt thou mar the corners of thy beard.' This prohibition focuses on rounding specific parts of the hair and beard, not general shaving or dyeing.

questions.question: What is forbidden in Leviticus 19:28 in relation to mourning practices?
options: Making cuttings in your flesh for the dead
Wearing black clothes
Fasting for more than three days
Offering sacrifices for the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Making cuttings in your flesh for the dead
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:28 forbids making cuttings in the flesh or printing marks upon the body as part of mourning rituals, which was a common pagan practice. This was a way to keep Israel distinct.

questions.question: Leviticus 19:29 warns against what specific social evil involving daughters?
options: Prostituting your daughter
Neglecting your daughter’s education
Forcing daughters into early marriage
Disinheriting daughters
questions.correctAnswer: Prostituting your daughter
questions.explanation: The verse warns, 'Do not prostitute thy daughter, to cause her to be a whore; lest the land fall to whoredom, and the land become full of wickedness,' condemning the act of forcing daughters into prostitution.

questions.question: What two key practices are commanded in Leviticus 19:30?
options: Keep the sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary
Offer daily sacrifices and keep festivals
Honor parents and love neighbors
Observe dietary laws and purity rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:30 commands the Israelites to 'keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary,' emphasizing worshipfulness and holy time observance.

questions.question: Leviticus 19:31 instructs the people to avoid what kinds of practices?
options: Seeking familiar spirits and wizards
Eating unclean animals
Engaging in dishonest business
Ignoring the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking familiar spirits and wizards
questions.explanation: Verse 31 says, 'Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards,' forbidding occult practices that defile the people.

questions.question: What attitude towards the elderly is commanded in Leviticus 19:32?
options: Rise up before the hoary head and honor the old man
Ignore the old because they are weak
Only respect the old if wealthy
Provide financial support only
questions.correctAnswer: Rise up before the hoary head and honor the old man
questions.explanation: The verse commands respect for elders: 'Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man,' linking this respect to fearing God.

questions.question: How should one treat a stranger dwelling in the land according to Leviticus 19:33-34?
options: Do not vex the stranger and love him as yourself
Ignore the stranger’s needs
Expel the stranger
Charge the stranger high taxes
questions.correctAnswer: Do not vex the stranger and love him as yourself
questions.explanation: Verses 33 and 34 instruct kindness to strangers, treating them as native-born and loving them as oneself, recalling Israel’s own experience as strangers in Egypt.

questions.question: What is emphasized in Leviticus 19:35-36 regarding business and justice?
options: Use just balances, weights, and measures
Charge interest on loans
Favor the rich in judgment
Disregard honesty for profit
questions.correctAnswer: Use just balances, weights, and measures
questions.explanation: These verses stress honest trade and judgment with just instruments to reflect God's justice and faithfulness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar command to love your neighbor as yourself, as seen in Leviticus 19:18?
options: Deuteronomy
Genesis
Exodus
Numbers
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:5 and 10:19 also command love for neighbor and stranger, echoing the ethical teaching of Leviticus 19:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage quotes Leviticus 19:18 when teaching about love?
options: Matthew 22:39
Acts 2:38
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 22:39
questions.explanation: Jesus cites the command to 'love thy neighbour as thyself' in Matthew 22:39, directly referencing Leviticus 19:18 as foundational for Christian ethics.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning is significant in Leviticus 19:2 where God commands to be 'holy'?
options: Qadosh, meaning set apart or consecrated
Shema, meaning hear
Shalom, meaning peace
Chesed, meaning mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Qadosh, meaning set apart or consecrated
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Qadosh' used in Leviticus 19:2 means 'holy' in the sense of being set apart or consecrated to God.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Leviticus 19:2 and 19:37 where God emphasizes holiness and obedience?
options: Inclusio framing the chapter with holiness and obedience
Chiasm focusing on sacrifice
Parallelism about judgment
Metaphor comparing Israel to a vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the chapter with holiness and obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 37 form an inclusio, framing the chapter by stressing God's holiness and the call for Israel to obey His statutes, creating literary unity.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:31 encourages seeking guidance from familiar spirits and wizards.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:31 explicitly forbids regarding those with familiar spirits or seeking wizards, stating 'Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards.'

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 19:18 commands to love your neighbor as yourself and forbids bearing a grudge or taking revenge.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:18 states, 'Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge ... but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself,' emphasizing love and forgiveness.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:26, which practice is forbidden alongside eating anything with blood?
options: Using enchantment and observing times
Eating unclean animals
Offering sacrifices without blood
Drinking wine during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Using enchantment and observing times
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:26 forbids eating blood, using enchantments, and observing certain times—likely pagan rituals—to maintain purity.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily revealed in the command for Israel to be holy as God is holy?
options: God's Holiness
God's Omnipotence
God's Mercy
God's Omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: God's Holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:2 states, 'Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy,' directly revealing God's attribute of holiness as the standard for His people.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:9-10, what social doctrine is taught by leaving the corners of fields and gleanings for the poor and stranger?
options: Doctrine of Social Justice
Doctrine of Divine Sovereignty
Doctrine of Justification
Doctrine of Atonement
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Social Justice
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:9-10 commands leaving portions of the harvest for the poor and stranger, teaching God's concern for social justice and care for the marginalized.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Leviticus 19:11 and 19:13 teach about interpersonal ethics?
options: Prohibition of stealing, lying, defrauding, and withholding wages
Mandate for ritual purification before judgment
Necessity of animal sacrifices for forgiveness
Command to honor only the mighty in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Prohibition of stealing, lying, defrauding, and withholding wages
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:11 forbids stealing, falsehood, and lying, while verse 13 forbids defrauding neighbors and withholding wages, collectively teaching the ethical requirement of honesty and fairness in community life.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 19:12 reveal God's concern regarding His name, and what does this imply about His character?
options: God's holiness and demand for reverence: do not swear falsely by His name
God's omnipresence: He is everywhere
God's patience: He tolerates sin indefinitely
God's sovereignty: He controls all nations
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and demand for reverence: do not swear falsely by His name
questions.explanation: Verse 12 prohibits false swearing by God's name, emphasizing God's holiness and the imperative that His name is not profaned, reflecting His pure and reverent character.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle about judgment is taught in Leviticus 19:15 regarding partiality?
options: Impartiality in judgment regardless of social status
Preference for the wealthy in courts
Judges should respect the mighty over the poor
Judgment should be delayed until sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Impartiality in judgment regardless of social status
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:15 commands judges to do no unrighteousness by respecting neither poor nor mighty but judging neighbors righteously, teaching impartiality and justice in judgment.

questions.question: What synthesis of Leviticus 19:17 and 19:18 highlights the proper Christian response to sin within the community?
options: Do not hate your brother but rebuke him and love your neighbor, avoiding vengeance
Avoid all confrontation with sinners to maintain peace
Revenge is allowed if one is wronged
Ignore sin to prevent judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Do not hate your brother but rebuke him and love your neighbor, avoiding vengeance
questions.explanation: Verses 17 and 18 together teach not to hate but to rebuke neighbors to prevent sin, and to love neighbors as oneself without seeking revenge, revealing God's call for holiness and love in community.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:19, what theological principle is taught by forbidding mixing different kinds in animals, seeds, and garments?
options: Doctrine of Separation and Purity
Doctrine of Atonement
Doctrine of Election
Doctrine of Resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Separation and Purity
questions.explanation: Verse 19 prohibits mixing species and fabrics, symbolizing God's demand for separation and purity in the life of His covenant people, reflecting holiness.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 19:20-22 teach about God's justice and mercy in the case of a man lying with a bondmaid betrothed to another man?
options: Scourging and a trespass offering, but not death, showing justice tempered with mercy
Immediate death penalty for both parties
No punishment required if she is not free
Only the woman is punished
questions.correctAnswer: Scourging and a trespass offering, but not death, showing justice tempered with mercy
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 prescribe scourging and a trespass offering but no death, indicating God's justice in punishing sin yet mercy in sparing lives when the woman was not free, illustrating the balance of God's attributes.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 19:23-25 collectively reveal God's providence and the principle of sanctification in agriculture?
options: First three years' fruit is 'uncircumcised' and not eaten, the fourth year is holy, and the fifth year is for eating and increase
All fruit must be eaten immediately upon harvest
Fruit must be offered as sacrifice every year
No special treatment of fruit is required
questions.correctAnswer: First three years' fruit is 'uncircumcised' and not eaten, the fourth year is holy, and the fifth year is for eating and increase
questions.explanation: These verses teach a pattern of sanctification and divine blessing on fruit trees, reflecting God's providential care and the principle of consecration over time.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the prohibition in Leviticus 19:26 against eating anything with blood and using enchantments or observing times?
options: It emphasizes God's holiness and rejection of pagan practices
It permits all magical practices
It commands strict fasting every month
It allows flexible dietary laws
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes God's holiness and rejection of pagan practices
questions.explanation: Verse 26 forbids eating blood and engaging in enchantments or astrology, underscoring God's demand for holiness and separation from pagan rituals.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 19:28, what does the prohibition against making cuttings in the flesh or marks upon the body reveal about Israel's identity?
options: They are set apart as God's holy people and not to imitate pagan mourning customs
They must tattoo their bodies as a sign of covenant
They should adopt all surrounding customs
They must mark themselves for tribal identification
questions.correctAnswer: They are set apart as God's holy people and not to imitate pagan mourning customs
questions.explanation: Verse 28 forbids bodily markings associated with pagan rites, emphasizing Israel's call to be holy and distinct from surrounding nations.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 19:30 teach about the relationship between observing the sabbaths and reverencing the sanctuary in relation to God's identity?
options: Both are acts of obedience that acknowledge the LORD as holy and sovereign
They are optional cultural customs
Only reverencing the sanctuary is required
Observing sabbaths is unrelated to God's holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Both are acts of obedience that acknowledge the LORD as holy and sovereign
questions.explanation: Verse 30 links sabbath observance and reverence for the sanctuary with recognizing the LORD's holiness and authority.

questions.question: How do Leviticus 19:33-34 collectively express a doctrine regarding the treatment of strangers among God's people?
options: Strangers should be loved as natives because Israel was once strangers in Egypt
Strangers should be excluded and mistreated
Strangers must pay tribute to Israel
Strangers are to be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers should be loved as natives because Israel was once strangers in Egypt
questions.explanation: These verses command love and fair treatment of strangers, grounding this in Israel's own experience of sojourning in Egypt, teaching compassion and solidarity.

questions.question: What apologist claim is addressed by Leviticus 19:35-36 regarding just weights and measures, and what does the text teach in response?
options: Sceptics claim ancient laws were arbitrary, but Leviticus 19:35-36 teaches God demands justice and honesty in commerce
Sceptics claim God condones dishonesty, but the text praises cheating
Sceptics say laws are irrelevant, but the text commands idolatry
Sceptics say God ignores fairness, but the text is silent on the topic
questions.correctAnswer: Sceptics claim ancient laws were arbitrary, but Leviticus 19:35-36 teaches God demands justice and honesty in commerce
questions.explanation: These verses command just balances and weights, showing that God's laws uphold fairness and integrity, countering claims of arbitrariness.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight emerges from combining Leviticus 19:4 and 19:31 about the exclusivity of worship and rejection of occult practices?
options: God demands exclusive worship of Him and forbids seeking familiar spirits and wizards
God permits worship of idols alongside Him
Witchcraft is endorsed as a valid spiritual practice
Idolatry is allowed if done secretly
questions.correctAnswer: God demands exclusive worship of Him and forbids seeking familiar spirits and wizards
questions.explanation: Verse 4 forbids idolatry, and verse 31 forbids seeking familiar spirits, emphasizing God's exclusive claim to worship and prohibition of occult practices.
